title: Regional preference optimizer: heterogeneous GPU selection, spot budget soft-caps, and graceful eviction fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: requests currently take the nearest-region / cheapest-GPU heuristic without a coordinated budget guardrail, which causes bursty spot usage, unexpected evictions, and opaque cost spikes for customers with mixed traffic patterns. We need a routing layer that balances cost (spot vs on-demand), GPU capability (A100 vs H100 vs T4), and region/tier preferences while enforcing per-customer soft budget caps and graceful fallbacks to compatible model variants when spot capacity is reclaimed.

Objective: build a 'regional preference optimizer' in the smart router that: 1) computes a cost-latency score per candidate endpoint (region + tier + GPU class), 2) applies per-customer budget soft-caps (both short-term and daily windows), 3) prefers high-capacity compatible GPU classes for high-throughput workloads, 4) honors regional data locality and policy, and 5) provides transparent telemetry and an opt-out feature flag.

Scope: routing policy and controller changes (router service + decision engine + policy config). Includes control-plane API for per-customer soft-cap config, runtime admission checks, and fallback logic to model variants (quantized/low-memory) or on-demand capacity. Does NOT include: hardware procurement, billing product changes (billing will use existing events), or per-model re-training.

Non-goals: building a full quota UI (we will expose metrics and API only), rewriting job-scheduler, or changing KV cache semantics in this ticket (we will instrument cache hit delta as a signal).
acceptance_criteria: Router computes a normalized cost-latency score and makes consistent choices under load in canary region (us-west1)
Per-customer short window soft-cap (configurable in control plane) prevents spot routing above threshold and triggers graceful fallback with <2% user-visible error increase
Fallback flows to compatible model variants without cache corruption; token-level cost differential reported in telemetry
End-to-end canary shows no >5% regression in p50 latency and <10% increase in token-cost for the average request across canary users
Feature gated behind 'regional-preference-optimizer' flag and can be rolled back cleanly within 10 minutes
comments: 2025-02-10 Maya Chen: Triage complete. High-level design sketched in Confluence. Recommend starting with single-region canary (us-west1) and single model family (redwood-3-small).

2025-02-12 Arjun Patel: Architecture review: added score components: base GPU cost per-token, estimated p50 latency delta, cold-KV penalty multiplier, and regional egress cost factor. Need to define weights and a small ML model for weight tuning later.

2025-02-14 SRE (Lena O'Connor): Observability checklist added: per-routing decision trace_id, metric: routing.fallback.rate, metrics: cost_per_token_by_route, spot_eviction_count, and dashboard links. Need limit on span cardinality.

2025-02-16 Arjun Patel: Prototype done. Bench results on synthetic workload: with soft-cap=15% of traffic, spot eviction rate dropped by 28% and cost per-token increased by 6% on average. p99 latency unchanged. Pushed RFC PR for review.
2025-02-20 PM (Diego Alvarez): Reviewed UX notes: expose soft-cap as short_window_pct and daily_budget_pct. PM asks for migration plan for existing customers with custom routing rules.

2025-02-21 Maya Chen: Security and compliance reviewed flags. Decided to mark security_review_required=false for this phase; future work will require KMS checks for private deployments. Next: finish canary rollout automation and add rollback playbook.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter soft-caps reduce cost but increase on-demand usage; we prefer soft enforcement with throttling and graceful fallbacks rather than hard rejects.
Weighting: start with deterministic weights (cost-per-token normalized, estimated p50 latency impact, eviction-risk score). Consider learning weights from labeled A/B data in a follow-up.

Fallback ordering: 1) compatible quantized model variant in same region/tier, 2) on-demand in same region, 3) compatible variant in nearest region (respecting data locality), 4) fail closed to on-demand if policy forbids cross-region routing.
Telemetry: emit routing.decisions.{route_id}.reason codes and decision_score for offline analysis; ensure privacy for customer identifiers in public dashboards.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary (5% traffic for 48h), expand to 20% for 72h with synthetic spike tests, then gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring gates. Immediate rollback on increased 5xx or >10% latency regression.
